name: 162. Bedrock passthrough for operations without native routes (bedrock passthrough fixture)
description: Local fixture regression, no network traffic leaves the machine. Run tests/e2e/api/runners/bedrock-endpoint-fixture.mjs --app-dir <dir> (it writes config.json: one Bedrock key with throwaway credentials in us-west-2, every Bedrock service endpoint overridden to the fixture, the fixture CA as network_config.ca_cert_pem, and the pricing datasheet URLs pointed at the fixture so the gateway starts offline), then start an isolated gateway with -app-dir <dir> and HTTPS_PROXY set to a dead port as a tripwire (the Bedrock client honours HTTPS_PROXY, and loopback is exempt, so only an accidental external call would fail), and run with bedrockEndpointFixture=1; every case is skipped otherwise. /bedrock_passthrough forwards exactly three AWS operations Bifrost has no native route for: InvokeAgent and knowledge-base Retrieve (bedrock-agent-runtime, fixture port 8796) and ApplyGuardrail (bedrock-runtime, fixture port 8798). The cases assert the request is SigV4 signed by the gateway for the key region and the bedrock service, that caller credentials and x-bf headers are not forwarded, that the upstream body, status, Content-Type and AWS error headers come back verbatim, and that every other path, a traversal and a non-POST method are refused with a 400 before any request is built. The /bedrock_passthrough/ bodies are carved out of the generic shape check in __skipShape because they are not inference responses.

item.name: 162.1 bedrock passthrough InvokeAgent is signed, forwarded to agent-runtime and the event stream returns untouched (bedrock agents)

exec: pm.test('the upstream content type and request id reach the caller', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type')).to.include('application/vnd.amazon.eventstream'); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Amzn-Requestid')).to.equal('req-agent'); });

pm.test('the event-stream bytes come back as AWS sent them', function () { var b = pm.response.stream; pm.expect(b[3], 'not the fixture event stream').to.equal(24); pm.expect(Buffer.from(b).toString('utf8')).to.include('fixture-event'); });
pm.test('exactly one request reached the service endpoint', function () { pm.expect(calls.length, JSON.stringify(calls.map(function (c) { return c.port + c.path; }))).to.equal(1); });
var call = calls[0] || { port: 0, path: '', headers: {}, body: '' };

pm.test('it went to the bedrock-agent-runtime endpoint', function () { pm.expect(call.port).to.equal(8796); pm.expect(call.path).to.match(/^\/agents\/AGENT123456\/agentAliases\/ALIAS12345\/sessions\/sess-1\/text$/); });

pm.test('it is SigV4 signed by the gateway for the key region and the bedrock service', function () { pm.expect(call.headers.authorization, JSON.stringify(call.headers)).to.match(/^AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=AKIAFIXTUREEXAMPLE0\/\d{8}\/us-west-2\/bedrock\/aws4_request/); pm.expect(call.headers['x-amz-date']).to.be.a('string'); });

pm.test('caller credentials and gateway headers are not forwarded', function () { pm.expect(call.headers.authorization).to.not.include('attacker'); pm.expect(call.headers['x-amz-security-token']).to.equal(undefined); pm.expect(Object.keys(call.headers).filter(function (h) { return h.indexOf('x-bf-') === 0; }), JSON.stringify(call.headers)).to.eql([]); });
pm.test('the request body is forwarded intact', function () { pm.expect(JSON.parse(call.body)).to.eql({ inputText: 'hi' }); });

item.name: 162.4 [EXPECT-404] bedrock passthrough returns an upstream not-found verbatim with its AWS error headers (bedrock agents)

exec: pm.test('status, body and exception type are AWS\'s own', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ message: 'agent not found' }); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Amzn-Errortype')).to.include('ResourceNotFoundException'); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Amzn-Requestid')).to.equal('req-missing'); });

item.name: 162.5 [EXPECT-400] bedrock passthrough refuses model invocation, which is not an allow-listed operation (bedrock passthrough allow-list)

exec: pm.test('the refusal is the Bedrock passthrough allow-list, and names the three operations it forwards', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include('bedrock passthrough only forwards POST InvokeAgent, Retrieve and ApplyGuardrail requests'); });
pm.test('nothing reached AWS', function () { pm.expect(calls.length, JSON.stringify(calls.map(function (c) { return c.path; }))).to.equal(0); });

item.name: 162.10 [EXPECT-400] bedrock passthrough refuses InvokeAgent for a key that holds only a Bedrock API key, which AWS does not accept for Agents Runtime (bedrock api key agents)

exec: pm.test('the refusal tells the operator to use a key with AWS credentials', function () { var j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.is_bifrost_error, pm.response.text()).to.equal(true); pm.expect(j.error.message, pm.response.text()).to.include('AWS credentials'); pm.expect(j.error.message).to.include('InvokeAgent'); });
pm.test('nothing reached AWS', function () { pm.expect(calls.length, JSON.stringify(calls.map(function (c) { return c.path; }))).to.equal(0); });

item.name: 162.11 bedrock passthrough ApplyGuardrail sends the same API-key-only key as a bearer token, because it is a bedrock-runtime operation (bedrock api key guardrails)

exec: pm.test('the guardrail verdict comes back', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().action).to.equal('NONE'); });

pm.test('exactly one request reached the bedrock-runtime endpoint', function () { pm.expect(calls.length, JSON.stringify(calls.map(function (c) { return c.port + c.path; }))).to.equal(1); pm.expect(calls[0].port).to.equal(8798); });

pm.test('it carries the Bedrock API key as a bearer token and is not SigV4 signed', function () { pm.expect(calls[0].headers.authorization).to.equal('Bearer fixture-bedrock-api-key'); pm.expect(calls[0].headers['x-amz-date']).to.equal(undefined); });

item.name: 162.12 bedrock passthrough InvokeAgent streams a slow agent run that outlives the gateway's 3s default request timeout, delivering every piece (bedrock agents streaming)

exec: pm.test('the upstream content type and request id reach the caller', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type')).to.include('application/vnd.amazon.eventstream'); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Amzn-Requestid')).to.equal('req-slow'); });

pm.test('all five pieces of the event stream arrive', function () { var body = Buffer.from(pm.response.stream).toString('utf8'); [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].forEach(function (n) { pm.expect(body, 'missing piece ' + n).to.include('slow-chunk-' + n + '|'); }); });

pm.test('the run lasted longer than the 3s default request timeout, so a total-duration cap is not applied to the stream', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime, 'finished in ' + pm.response.responseTime + 'ms').to.be.above(3500); });

item.name: 162.13 [EXPECT-500] bedrock passthrough Retrieve on a knowledge-base id containing the word stream is still cut off by the request timeout (bedrock knowledge bases)

exec: pm.test('the 4s Retrieve is cut off by the 3s request timeout, not streamed through', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.equal(500); var j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.is_bifrost_error, pm.response.text()).to.equal(true); pm.expect(j.error.error, pm.response.text()).to.include('context deadline exceeded'); });
pm.test('it was refused before the 4s upstream finished', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime, 'finished in ' + pm.response.responseTime + 'ms').to.be.below(3900); });
